A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same RADD study and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–K. Their equations, algorithms, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original RADD language-modeling results, sampling-time and entropy measurements, generation-order experiments, and generated examples in Section 4 and Appendices J–K.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–7, the sampling curves in Figure 1, and generated examples in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: The RADD components, objectives, and cached sampling procedures are unchanged. Appendix J.1 changes 'encoder-only' to 'decoder-only' but retains the same layer description and explicit lack of an attention mask; this relabeling does not establish an implemented architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on OpenWebText and evaluate on LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103, and One Billion Words. Unconditional generation, conditional generation, and generation-order scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Tables 1–2 retain GPT-2, D3PM, PLAID, and the SEDD variants in their respective comparisons. Appendix J retains the same SEDD comparator for sampling evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, hyperparameters, data processing, sampling steps, precision settings, batch sizes, sample counts, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Hardware descriptions become less specific, but no replacement experimental setting or rerun is reported.

E4.justification: The scaling, time-conditioning, and loss comparisons in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. Appendix J retains the precision analysis, batch-size timing ablation, generation-order study, and extended-training evaluation without new or removed analyses.

E5.justification: The averaging procedures remain unchanged. Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training seed counts, and v4 introduces no new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7, plotted results, and generated examples are retained. For example, Table 2 still reports RADD-DSE WikiText2 perplexity of 29.17, and Table 3 retains the 4096-step RADD-medium sampling time of 18.20 seconds.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, their proofs, mathematical definitions, and the reverse-process and expected-NFE derivations are unchanged. Revised appendix-reference wording and minor grammar edits do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about score factorization, time-independent parameterization, caching acceleration, objective equivalence, and performance on five language-modeling benchmarks.

C2.justification: The interpretations of precision effects, caching efficiency, and generation order are unchanged, as are the GPT-2-scale and fixed-length-output limitations. Replacing 'GPU utilization' with 'hardware utilization' preserves the same batch-size saturation argument.

D1.justification: v4 removes hardware specificity: Appendix J.2 replaces the 32 V100 32G GPU setup with generic multi-accelerator nodes; Table 3 replaces the NVIDIA A800 80G GPU with a high-memory accelerator; Table 5 removes the NVIDIA 4090 identifier while retaining 24GB memory. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against previous and concurrent research are unchanged. The Campbell et al. (2022) citation changes grammatical format without changing attribution or comparison.

P1.justification: Many internal references change from 'Appendix' to 'Section,' alongside minor grammar, citation-syntax, architecture-label, and hardware-terminology edits. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 5 have revised hardware wording in their captions, with limited local text reflow elsewhere. Figure content, plotted curves, table structure, highlighting, and placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific results and theory are retained, but removing the training GPU specifications and timing-device identities in Appendix J.2 and Tables 3 and 5 weakens reproducibility and the interpretation of runtime claims. The small editorial refinements do not offset this limited loss of experimental transparency.
